model.name: super_ambient: preliminary architecture
model.documentation: Preliminary ArchiMate model of the super_ambient demo (synthetic-data FHIR patient workspace with ambient documentation and Jev classification). Generated from the code; not reviewed. See the accompanying PDF for the narrative.

element.name: Clinician
element.documentation: Reads patient data and documents consultations; the intended end user.

element.name: Application owner and developer
element.documentation: Decides scope, approves plans and runs the live evaluations.

element.name: Medical doctor (domain reviewer)
element.documentation: Not yet involved in review. Will advise on blood pressure pairing and clinical labels.

element.name: Employer IT (future Azure tenant)
element.documentation: Will host the application in a later phase.

element.name: Documentation workload and scattered patient data
element.documentation: Clinicians spend time finding data and writing notes.

element.name: Understand the patient's situation quickly
element.documentation: Ask questions in plain language and get source-grounded answers.

element.name: Document the consultation smoothly
element.documentation: Turn a conversation into a reviewable note and structured suggestions.

element.name: Show where smart classification helps, safely
element.documentation: Use Jev as a classifier inside strict, human-reviewed boundaries.

element.name: Human approval before anything is saved
element.documentation: Proposals start unreviewed; edits revoke approval; the save path re-checks everything.

element.name: Answers and proposals trace to a source
element.documentation: Facts carry resource id and field; proposals carry an exact transcript quote.

element.name: The application, not a model, builds FHIR
element.documentation: Typed builders produce every saved resource; model output is never sent as a bundle.

element.name: Secrets and keys stay on the server
element.documentation: Keys are read from server-side environment variables only; errors never carry them.

element.name: Synthetic data only (public, unauthenticated test server)
element.documentation: The public HAPI server has no privacy and is wiped periodically.

element.name: Sending transcript text to a third party is opt-in
element.documentation: LLM_STRUCTURING=jev is off by default and warns in the UI.

element.name: Patient and encounter context enforced on every read and write
element.documentation: Returned and followed resources are checked against the selected patient; writes only for demo-tagged patients.

element.name: Works without a model service (visible mock mode)
element.documentation: Default provider is a rule-based mock that is labelled as such.

element.name: Clinician
element.documentation: The person using the workspace.

element.name: Treating clinician
element.documentation: Role that asks, records, reviews and saves.

element.name: Ask about patient data
element.documentation: Pose a question, read the answer with its source observations.

element.name: Record and document a consultation
element.documentation: Record or paste a rehearsal conversation and build a note draft.

element.name: Review and approve proposals
element.documentation: Edit, approve or reject each structured suggestion and the note.

element.name: Save approved content to the EHR
element.documentation: Preview, save as one transaction, and read the resources back.

element.name: Patient information retrieval
element.documentation: Answers to questions about the selected patient.

element.name: Consultation documentation
element.documentation: Draft note and structured proposals from a conversation.

element.name: Visit note
element.documentation: The consultation note (käyntimerkintä); saved as a DocumentReference with docStatus preliminary.

element.name: Patient record
element.documentation: The patient's data held in the EHR (the public HAPI server in the demo).

element.name: Web UI
element.documentation: React client: patient and visit selection, Ask view, recording and documentation view.

element.name: Workspace shell
element.documentation: Persistent context bar, patient search, encounter picker, status and seeding panels; guards against stale responses.

element.name: Ask view
element.documentation: Question box, answer, source facts, search plan and technical details.

element.name: Recording and documentation view
element.documentation: Audio capture, transcript editor, sample conversations, proposal table, preview, save and read-back.

element.name: Application server
element.documentation: Server-side logic in Next.js route handlers and the lib/ modules; holds all secrets and external connections.

element.name: API layer (route handlers)
element.documentation: Validates request bodies with strict schemas and delegates to the services.

element.name: Question answering
element.documentation: Interprets a question, runs allow-listed read searches, extracts facts and composes a grounded answer.

element.name: Question interpreter
element.documentation: Maps a question to an information need: Jev classification or keyword mock.

element.name: Transcript structuring
element.documentation: Turns a transcript into a note draft and proposals. Mock rules by default; Jev classifies sentences when LLM_STRUCTURING=jev.

element.name: Review and approval engine
element.documentation: Approval hashes, staleness, allowed FHIR targets and validation of structuring output.

element.name: Save service
element.documentation: Server-side re-check, preview, validation, one transaction with conditional create, read-back and timeout recovery.

element.name: FHIR builders and patient guard
element.documentation: Allow-listed search builders, typed resource builders and the patient-scope guard.

element.name: EHR adapter (HAPI R4, Epic)
element.documentation: EhrAdapter interface and its R4 implementation: paging, limits, retries, capability check, optional Bearer token. One shared instance for sources without login; a new instance per request for sources with login.

element.name: FHIR source registry
element.documentation: The only place that defines a source: address, login type, write permission and patient-search form. The browser sends only a source id; unknown ids are rejected and read-only sources refuse writes.

element.name: SMART login and session
element.documentation: Authorization code flow with PKCE (S256) as a public client; endpoints discovered from the server and restricted to its origin. The access token lives in an httpOnly cookie that only the server reads; no server-side session store.

element.name: Language adapter
element.documentation: Selects mock, Jev hybrid or unavailable and reports per capability who does what.

element.name: Jev client
element.documentation: Timeout, bounded retries, strict response parsing; errors never carry key or text.

element.name: Demo data seeding
element.documentation: User-triggered upload of the app's own synthetic fixtures (second write path next to the save service).

element.name: Transcription adapter
element.documentation: Interface for speech-to-text; no provider is wired, so transcripts are pasted by hand.

element.name: Configuration and service wiring
element.documentation: Reads environment settings and creates the adapters.

element.name: Evaluation and smoke tooling
element.documentation: Eval scripts (mock and live Jev), HAPI smoke test and browser walkthrough.

element.name: Automated tests (Vitest)
element.documentation: Unit and integration tests against an in-memory FHIR fake and a scripted Jev; no UI or route tests.

element.name: Internal REST/JSON API (/api/*)
element.documentation: The only interface between browser and server.

element.name: Patient data question service
element.documentation: POST /api/ask.

element.name: Transcript structuring service
element.documentation: POST /api/structure.

element.name: Documentation save service
element.documentation: POST /api/save/preview, /api/save and /api/read.

element.name: EHR access service
element.documentation: Patient, encounter and resource reads and the write transaction.

element.name: Information need
element.documentation: Strict schema: intent, resource types, time range, scope. Never contains a URL or patient.

element.name: Fact (source-grounded)
element.documentation: A value or statement with resource id, fields and clinical time.

element.name: Transcript
element.documentation: Speaker-labelled segments with a content version.

element.name: Proposal
element.documentation: Reviewable suggestion: type, value, exact source quote, certainty, review status.

element.name: Note draft
element.documentation: Reason, history, findings, assessment and plan sections.

element.name: Transaction bundle and snapshot
element.documentation: The previewed bundle and the hash the server re-checks.

element.name: FHIR resources
element.documentation: Patient, Encounter, Observation, Condition, DocumentReference and read-only types.

element.name: Demo fixtures
element.documentation: Two synthetic patients with visits, vitals, labs, medication, allergy, problem and a report.

element.name: Sample conversations and gold sets
element.documentation: 14 synthetic conversations and question sets; written by an AI, not reviewed by a doctor.

element.name: Clinician's browser
element.documentation: Runs the React client; captures audio locally and keeps it in memory.

element.name: Browser audio capture (MediaRecorder)
element.documentation: Audio is never sent to HAPI; it goes to a transcription service only on an explicit action.

element.name: Client JavaScript bundle
element.documentation: Output of next build.

element.name: Access-token cookie (httpOnly)
element.documentation: Holds the OAuth access token for a source that needs login (about one hour). SameSite=Strict, Secure on https; unreadable by page scripts.

element.name: Developer workstation (Linux)
element.documentation: bun run dev; no Node installed, Bun runs everything.

element.name: Bun runtime and package manager
element.documentation: bun@1.4.2, bun.lock.

element.name: Next.js 16 and React 19
element.documentation: App Router with cacheComponents.

element.name: Vercel hosting (current)
element.documentation: Hosts the deployed demo; not protected by login unless Deployment Protection is on.

element.name: Next.js server runtime
element.documentation: Serverless functions; capability cache is per instance.

element.name: Next.js server build
element.documentation: Route handlers and server modules.

element.name: Server environment configuration
element.documentation: Host environment variables or a local env file; holds the Jev key and the Epic client id.

element.name: Employer Azure tenant (planned)
element.documentation: Target hosting; may also run an ICD-API VM.

element.name: HAPI FHIR public test server
element.documentation: https://hapi.fhir.org/baseR4; shared, unauthenticated, wiped periodically.

element.name: FHIR R4 REST API
element.documentation: Search, read, $validate and transaction.

element.name: Epic on FHIR sandbox
element.documentation: https://fhir.epic.com/interconnect-fhir-oauth; synthetic test patients, login with documented test users; the app reads only.

element.name: Epic FHIR R4 API
element.documentation: Patient (demographics search needs a birth date with the name), Encounter, Observation and other reads.

element.name: Epic SMART / OAuth 2.0 service
element.documentation: authorize and token endpoints from .well-known/smart-configuration; PKCE S256, standalone launch, public client.

element.name: Typesafe AI cloud (Jev)
element.documentation: https://api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone; data-processing terms not yet checked.

element.name: System One classification API
element.documentation: Typed questions (choice, score, noul) over a state; no text generation.

element.name: ICD-API service (local, systemd)
element.documentation: Runs on the owner's machine (port 8382); unreachable from Vercel.

element.name: ICD-11 search API
element.documentation: Possible future code suggestions; ICD-10 would be needed for production.

element.name: Internet (HTTPS)
element.documentation: All browser-to-server and server-to-service traffic.

element.name: Core workspace, HAPI adapter and save path
element.documentation: Delivered first version of the specification.

element.name: Jev question interpretation
element.documentation: Classifier-based interpretation with thresholds and an evaluation set.

element.name: Jev transcript structuring with clause splitting
element.documentation: Opt-in hybrid structuring; evaluation on synthetic gold set.

element.name: Agent guardrails (AGENTS.md, permissions, hook)
element.documentation: Project instructions, permission rules and an .env hook.

element.name: Second FHIR source: Epic sandbox (read-only, SMART login)
element.documentation: Source registry and selector, PKCE login with cookie session, Epic search shapes and test-patient list. Verified by the owner for login, patient search, encounters and questions on blood pressure, labs, allergies, medications, conditions, imaging reports, documents and the overview (medication names are read from the reference display; an imaging document is recognised from its type; Epic needs a category on Observation searches, so the overview splits observations into vitals and labs).

element.name: Verify all question types against Epic
element.documentation: Every question type has been tried by hand. Findings: Epic ignores _sort, requires a category or code on Observation searches and offers no MedicationStatement in R4 (403); the app reports the 403 on purpose and explains 401 and 403 clearly.

element.name: Epic login from the Vercel deployment
element.documentation: Callback URI registered at Epic, client id set in Vercel, code deployed. The owner confirmed that login works from the deployed app. Epic took about ten minutes to accept the new URI, and it compares the URI literally (https, exact path).

element.name: Held-out evaluation with doctor-written transcripts
element.documentation: The real accuracy check; the current sets are in-sample.

element.name: Question-and-answer pair handling
element.documentation: Short replies such as 'Ei.' need the preceding question.

element.name: Progress indication for structuring
element.documentation: About 300 ms per sentence at concurrency 1.

element.name: Migrate to the employer's Azure tenant
element.documentation: Hosting, secrets store, identity and network rules.

element.name: ICD-11 code suggestions
element.documentation: Nice-to-have; needs a Finnish-to-English vocabulary step.

element.name: Plateau 1: Vercel demo with Jev
element.documentation: Today's state.

element.name: Plateau 2: Azure-hosted demo
element.documentation: Target state, still a demo.

view.name: 1 Motivation
view.documentation: Why the application exists: stakeholders, the driver, goals, and the principles, requirements and constraints that shape the design.

view.name: 2 Business usage
view.documentation: How a clinician uses the application: the role, the four processes, the business services they realize, and the application services and views that support them.

view.name: 3 Application structure
view.documentation: Decomposition of the application: the web UI, the server-side modules with the source files they are built from, and the development tooling. Composition is shown by nesting.

view.name: 4 Application cooperation
view.documentation: Main information flows between the application components, and the external technology services they depend on (Jev, HAPI and Epic). Flows involving the configuration module are left out for readability; see the appendix.

view.name: 5 Information
view.documentation: Which components read and write which information objects, and how the data objects realize the business objects. Question answering also reads the FHIR resources (read access not drawn here; see the appendix). The FHIR resources are the only data persisted outside the application.

view.name: 6 Technology and deployment
view.documentation: Where the application runs and what it talks to. Planned and parked elements are drawn dashed. Node-to-node flows (browser to Vercel to HAPI and Typesafe) are in the model but not drawn here.

view.name: 7 Implementation and migration
view.documentation: What has been delivered, and what is planned or parked on the way from the Vercel demo to an Azure-hosted demo. Nothing here is committed scope.
